To solve this problem, we can use a breadth-first search (BFS) algorithm to find the shortest path in an unweighted grid. BFS is suitable because it explores all nodes at the present depth level before moving on to nodes at the next depth level, ensuring that the first time we reach the destination, it is via the shortest path.

We'll represent the grid as a 2D list and perform BFS starting from the position of the `*` (start point), moving only through `O` (open cells), and stopping when we reach the `#` (destination point). We'll track the path by keeping a record of the parent of each visited cell.

Here is the grid:

```
O O X O O O O X
O X X X X X X X
O * X X O X O O
O O # O O X O O
O O O X O O O X
O X O O O O O O
O O X X O O O O
```

After performing BFS and tracking the path, the shortest path from `*` to `#` is found to be:

<FINAL>right right down down left left left down down left down right</FINAL>
